ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sound is whispered, with no buzz in the throat? (1 mark)
   A. /g/
   B. /d/
   C. /v/
   D. /f/

2. What should you do before using a website for facts? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it without reading
   B. Believe everything
   C. Share your address
   D. Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere

3. Which noun needs the article 'the' because there is only one? (1 mark)
   A. boy
   B. chair
   C. mango
   D. sun

4. An invitation is (1 mark)
   A. a big meal
   B. a gift
   C. a song
   D. a card or message that asks a person to come to an event

5. A direct question is one whose answer (1 mark)
   A. is not in the text
   B. is a joke
   C. has no words
   D. is written in the text

6. What is the plural of 'church'? (1 mark)
   A. churches
   B. churchs
   C. churchen
   D. churchies

7. An open-ended composition (1 mark)
   A. has no words
   B. has only one correct answer
   C. gives you a topic and you decide the story
   D. must copy a story

8. What does 'proofread' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Copy from a book
   B. Write faster
   C. Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
   D. Draw pictures

9. What is a good way to find the meaning of an unknown word in a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Read the sentences around it for clues
   B. Skip the passage
   C. Guess without reading
   D. Ask a stranger

10. Which letter is silent in 'knife'? (1 mark)
   A. e
   B. k
   C. n
   D. f

11. The noun 'present' (a gift) is stressed on (1 mark)
   A. the first syllable
   B. the second syllable
   C. the last letter
   D. no syllable

12. A comic is a story told in (1 mark)
   A. a series of small pictures
   B. a table
   C. a single long word
   D. a mathematical sum

13. Which is a possessive pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. yourself
   B. yours
   C. your
   D. you

14. When reading silently, you should (1 mark)
   A. read quietly in your head
   B. read backwards
   C. sing
   D. shout

15. At the end of a yes or no question, the voice usually (1 mark)
   A. rises
   B. stays low always
   C. falls
   D. stops

16. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a conversation between two or more people
   B. a list of nouns
   C. a picture only
   D. a poem with no words

17. Why do two learners write different stories from the same pictures? (1 mark)
   A. Each writer uses different words and ideas
   B. One is always wrong
   C. They copy each other
   D. The pictures are blank

18. Which word begins with /v/? (1 mark)
   A. weed
   B. vegetables
   C. window
   D. wheat

19. Which pair of words differs only because of /v/ and /w/? (1 mark)
   A. bell and bill
   B. sip and chip
   C. vet and wet
   D. sit and sat

20. What is the contraction of 'cannot'? (1 mark)
   A. ca'nt
   B. cant
   C. can't
   D. cann't

21. Which word in this sentence is the adverb? 'The nurse spoke gently.' (1 mark)
   A. nurse
   B. gently
   C. spoke
   D. The

22. What does a referee do? (1 mark)
   A. Controls a game and makes sure the rules are followed
   B. Trains the team
   C. Cleans the field
   D. Sells tickets

23. Which is an example of a nonverbal cue? (1 mark)
   A. A word
   B. A song
   C. A sentence
   D. A thumbs-up

24. What is at the centre of a mind map? (1 mark)
   A. The date
   B. The last idea
   C. The author's name
   D. The main topic

25. Which word has the short vowel /ʌ/? (1 mark)
   A. door
   B. sport
   C. mother
   D. floor

26. When I arrived, the bus had left. Which happened first? (1 mark)
   A. I arrived.
   B. Both together.
   C. The bus left.
   D. Neither happened.

27. Which is a good way to start a diary entry sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Chapter One ...
   B. Yours faithfully ...
   C. Dear Sir ...
   D. Today I ...

28. Which word has a silent t? (1 mark)
   A. tent
   B. ten
   C. table
   D. listen

29. Which is a fact, not an opinion? (1 mark)
   A. Saving is a good idea.
   B. The club meets on Fridays.
   C. Everyone should join.
   D. The club is the best.

30. Which preposition means 'facing'? (1 mark)
   A. among
   B. between
   C. opposite
   D. behind

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write two polite phrases you could use in a conversation, one to add something and one to give the other person a turn. (2 marks)

32. Write a short dialogue of four lines in which you borrow a book from a friend politely. (4 marks)

33. Write four sentences using north, south, east and west to describe the position of places near your school. (4 marks)

34. Explain the rule for changing nouns that end in y into plurals. Give two examples. (3 marks)

35. Make two sentences with 'very ... but ...' about shopping. (2 marks)

36. Explain why 'She asked where the clinic was?' is wrong and correct it. (3 marks)

37. Write the -ing form of: run, sit, swim. (3 marks)

38. Write two words for each cluster: (a) br (b) gr. (4 marks)

39. Give one riddle about an object used for cleaning, with its answer. (2 marks)

40. Write the comparative and superlative of: happy, beautiful. (2 marks)

41. Explain when we use some and when we use any. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

42. Sort these adverbs into manner, time and place: quietly, later, nearby, always, neatly, upstairs. (3 marks)

43. Correct: (a) 'How much books are there?' (b) 'I do not have some money.' (2 marks)

44. Explain why we do not say 'I am knowing the answer'. Give the correct sentence. (3 marks)

45. Name three polite words or phrases and say when each is used. (3 marks)

46. Make a simple plan for a story called 'The Guests Who Came Late'. (4 marks)

47. Put the adjectives in the right order: a (red, round, big) balloon. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — /f/
   /f/ is a whispered sound. /v/, /d/ and /g/ are voiced.

2. D — Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   Checking a second source shows whether the fact is correct.

3. D — sun
   There is only one sun, so we say the sun.

4. D — a card or message that asks a person to come to an event
   An invitation invites someone to an event.

5. D — is written in the text
   Direct answers are stated plainly in the text.

6. A — churches
   Nouns ending in ch add es.

7. C — gives you a topic and you decide the story
   You use your own ideas to complete it.

8. C — Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
   Proofreading is checking spelling, punctuation and meaning.

9. A — Read the sentences around it for clues
   Context clues help you understand new words.

10. B — k
   We say nife, so the k is silent.

11. A — the first syllable
   The noun is PRE-sent and the verb is pre-SENT.

12. A — a series of small pictures
   Comics use pictures, often with speech bubbles.

13. B — yours
   Yours stands alone and shows ownership.

14. A — read quietly in your head
   Silent reading helps you focus.

15. A — rises
   Yes or no questions usually end with a rise.

16. A — a conversation between two or more people
   It shows what people say to each other.

17. A — Each writer uses different words and ideas
   Each writer has a different voice.

18. B — vegetables
   'Vegetables' begins with /v/, said with the top teeth on the lower lip.

19. C — vet and wet
   In 'vet' and 'wet' only the first sound differs.

20. C — can't
   'Cannot' becomes 'can't'.

21. B — gently
   'Gently' tells how she spoke.

22. A — Controls a game and makes sure the rules are followed
   A referee is the official in charge.

23. D — A thumbs-up
   Gestures are nonverbal.

24. D — The main topic
   The main topic is in the middle.

25. C — mother
   'Mother' has the short /ʌ/.

26. C — The bus left.
   The past perfect shows the earlier action.

27. D — Today I ...
   Diary sentences often start with 'Today I ...'.

28. D — listen
   'Listen' is said 'lisen'.

29. B — The club meets on Fridays.
   A fact can be checked.

30. C — opposite
   'The post office is opposite the bank.'

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: 'May I add something?' and 'What do you think?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable polite phrase.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: Good morning, Ali. B: Good morning. A: May I borrow your book, please? B: Yes, here you are. A: Thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for greeting, request, answer and thanks.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The gate is south of the classroom. The field is east of the gate. The library is west of the field. The road is north of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: If a consonant comes before y, change y to i and add es (baby, babies). If a vowel comes before y, add s (boy, boys).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for correct examples.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The mango is very sweet, but it is small. The bag is very nice, but it is expensive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reports a question, so it is a statement and needs a full stop. Correct: She asked where the clinic was.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reason, 1 for correction, 1 for full stop.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: running, sitting, swimming
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) bring, broom (or bread, brush) (b) green, grass (or grow, ground)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have hairs but no head, and I clean your teeth. What am I? A toothbrush.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear riddle and 1 for the correct answer.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: happier, happiest; more beautiful, most beautiful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Some is used in positive sentences and polite offers: I have some books. Any is used in questions and negatives: Do you have any books?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each example.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Manner: quietly, neatly. Time: later, always. Place: nearby, upstairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) How many books are there? (b) I do not have any money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Know' is a state verb, not an action in progress, so it is not normally used in the progressive form. The correct sentence is 'I know the answer.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for state verb explanation, 1 for the correct sentence, 1 for clear expression.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Please: when asking. Thank you: when someone helps. Sorry: when we make a mistake.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each phrase with its use.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: family prepares for a party. Middle: guests do not arrive, food gets cold. Problem: they lost the way. End: they arrive, everyone laughs and eats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a beginning, 1 for events, 1 for a problem and 1 for an ending.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: a big round red balloon
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size first and 1 mark for shape before colour.
